claims.text: One of the most popular Python web application frameworks.

claims.text: Many extensions provided by the community that make adding new functionality easy.

evidence.summary: The README and pyproject.toml files both explicitly mention that Flask offers suggestions but does not enforce dependencies, and there are many community extensions available to add functionality easily. The project layout is up to the developer. This directly supports the claim. [LLM verdict, confidence capped]

claims.text: A lightweight WSGI web application framework

evidence.summary: The README and pyproject.toml files both contain explicit statements that Flask is a lightweight WSGI web application framework, matching the claim verbatim. The pyproject.toml file also lists 'wsgi' in classifiers and explicitly includes required dependencies like Werkzeug (a WSGI library) which supports the technical truth of the claim. [LLM verdict, confidence capped]

claims.text: Designed to make getting started quick and easy, with the ability to scale up to complex applications.

evidence.summary: The README and pyproject.toml files together provide independent technical evidence that Flask is designed to make getting started quick and easy (e.g. the simple example app), while also being able to scale up to complex applications (e.g. optional dependencies for async, dotenv, pre-commit, tests). The project layout with src/, examples/, tests/ directories further supports this claim. [LLM verdict, confidence capped]

claims.text: Begun as a simple wrapper around Werkzeug and Jinja

evidence.summary: The project's pyproject.toml and file tree show that Flask was indeed started as a simple wrapper around Werkzeug (dependency listed in dependencies) and Jinja (another dependency). The README itself confirms this historical origin, but the technical evidence comes from the actual manifest files listing these core dependencies. [LLM verdict, confidence capped]

claims.text: Offers suggestions, but doesn't enforce any dependencies or project layout.

evidence.summary: The pyproject.toml shows Flask does not enforce dependencies or project layout; it lists only required and optional dependencies without enforcing any structure. The `dev` group includes tools like ruff, tox, pre-commit which are used for development but not runtime. The `[tool.flit.sdist]` excludes docs/_build/ showing the build process is separate from distribution. [LLM verdict, confidence capped]
